ov: Two species of ground-dwelling Australian birds, famous for mimicking sounds around them and for the male’s huge, lyre-shaped tail, fanned out in courtship. They are poor fliers that mostly just glide downhill.
wt: Females about 0.9 kg, males about 1.1 kg
rg: Eastern Australia: rainforests of Victoria, New South Wales and southeast Queensland; introduced to Tasmania.
df: Insects, spiders, earthworms and other invertebrates, sometimes lizards, frogs and seeds.
fx: In the breeding season males may sing for four hours a day.
Lyrebirds can live up to 30 years.
